nc7c5b7b9f7e.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: UDAY – Debt takeover by the States
ICEP-2024 in Andhra Pradesh – Target of 160 GW of renewable energy
PM JANMAN through AP DISCOMs – Electrification of 24,691 tribal households
nc7c5b7b9f7e.x: RDSS is a results-linked infrastructure and reform grant; electrification of 24,691 tribal households is linked with PM JANMAN through AP DISCOMs.

n66bc5b15fcf.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's power capacity and generation mix?
o: Non-fossil sources account for over 54% of installed capacity
Coal produces over 70% of electricity generation
Coal accounts for over 54% of installed capacity
Nuclear accounts for about 1.6% of capacity and about 3% of generation
n66bc5b15fcf.x: Coal is only about 42% of installed capacity; it is non-fossil sources that exceed 54%, even though coal gives over 70% of generation.

na0b454230c8.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: CERC – Central tariffs and inter-State matters
SERCs – State retail tariffs, licensing and standards
APTEL – Reports on installed capacity and National Electricity Plan
CEA – Reports on installed capacity and National Electricity Plan
na0b454230c8.x: APTEL hears appeals against CERC and SERC orders; technical reports such as the National Electricity Plan are published by the CEA.

n736f7ca57c2.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Sixteenth Finance Commission – Recommended active DISCOM privatisation by States
Odisha DISCOMs – Taken over by Torrent in 2020-21
n736f7ca57c2.x: Odisha's DISCOMs were taken over by Tata Power in 2020-21; Torrent is linked with the Bhiwandi franchise of 2007.

ne0000a9e550.s:
Assertion (A): Simhadri STPP is located in Visakhapatnam district.
Reason (R): Dr M.V.R. RTPP is located at Krishnapatnam in Nellore district.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
ne0000a9e550.x: Simhadri is in Visakhapatnam district, but Dr M.V.R. RTPP is at Muddanur, Kadapa district; Krishnapatnam has Sri Damodaram Sanjeevaiah TPS.

nfca4fbf46ac.s:
Assertion (A): Metering of distribution transformers, feeders and consumers is a component of DDUGJY.
Reason (R): DDUGJY also includes development of micro-grids and off-grid systems.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nfca4fbf46ac.x: Both are components of DDUGJY, but one component does not explain the other.

n58989ac4d44.s:
Assertion (A): India has four regional power grids.
Reason (R): The Southern Grid was synchronised in December 2013.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n58989ac4d44.x: India had five regional grids (Northern, Eastern, Western, North-Eastern and Southern); the Southern Grid was the last, synchronised in December 2013.

ndd3bcc80682.s: The Electricity Act, 2003 required State Electricity Boards to be:
o: Merged with the Central Electricity Authority
ndd3bcc80682.x: The Electricity Act, 2003 required SEBs to be unbundled, not to remain fully integrated.

n2a065cb2111.s: Which is the nodal agency for the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY)?
n2a065cb2111.x: REC is the nodal agency of DDUGJY (and of Saubhagya), not PFC.

n1d4de69d9f9.s: AT&C losses of DISCOMs fell from 22.62% in FY 2013-14 to ____ in FY 2024-25.
n1d4de69d9f9.x: AT&C losses fell from 22.62% in FY 2013-14 to 15.04% in FY 2024-25.

nf029b2f3d82.s: The Green Energy Corridor began in 2012 with a study by which organisation?
nf029b2f3d82.x: The Green Energy Corridor began with a PGCIL study in 2012 (not CEA) and was implemented from 2015.

n530153fd280.s: Which organisation signed an MoU with PNGRB for smart domestic PNG meters?
n530153fd280.x: EESL, which aggregates demand for large smart-metering programmes, signed an MoU with PNGRB for smart domestic PNG meters.

n3e86f94ed69.s: The National Generation Adequacy Plan projects India's peak demand in 2035-36 at:
n3e86f94ed69.x: The plan projects a peak demand of 459 GW in 2035-36, with 1,121 GW installed capacity.

n2832048f96e.s: The typical capacity factor of coal power plants in India is:
n2832048f96e.x: Coal plants operate at about 60–85%; 20–25% is solar and 20–35% is wind.

ndf17cf4ce2c.s: The nodal agencies of the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) are:
ndf17cf4ce2c.x: RDSS, a reform-based, results-linked scheme extended to FY 2027-28, has REC and PFC as nodal agencies.

n898a28f8e8b.s: The Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL) was established on:
n898a28f8e8b.x: APTEL was set up on 24 August 2004 under the Electricity Act 2003.

n72cbb39deeb.s: Andhra Pradesh, which has no coal of its own, draws coal for its thermal plants from:
n72cbb39deeb.x: Andhra Pradesh has no coal of its own and depends on Singareni and MCL.

n176ef49dc4f.s: The Andhra Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (APERC) was set up under:
n176ef49dc4f.x: APERC was set up under the AP Electricity Reform Act, 1998, which came before the Electricity Act 2003.

ne5225e03d35.s: The ACS-ARR gap of a DISCOM is calculated per unit as:
o: Average revenue realised minus average cost of supply
Average cost of supply minus average revenue realised
Average cost of supply minus AT&C loss
Average revenue realised minus AT&C loss
ne5225e03d35.x: The ACS-ARR gap is the average cost of supply minus the average revenue realised per unit.

n937b9062d21.s: The National Electricity Plan is a report of:
n937b9062d21.x: The National Electricity Plan is a CEA report; NITI Aayog is associated with India Energy Security Scenarios 2047.

nbd454688c91.s: States in India spend about ____ a year subsidising farm and domestic power.
nbd454688c91.x: States spend about ₹2.4 lakh crore a year on farm and domestic power subsidies.

nac7d6641e0e.s: HPX, a power exchange in India, stands for:
nac7d6641e0e.x: HPX is the Hindustan Power Exchange, one of India's power exchanges along with IEX and PXIL.

ncc830e02eb2.s: The Real-Time Market was introduced in India's power exchanges in:
ncc830e02eb2.x: The Real-Time Market began in 2020; the Green Day-Ahead Market followed in 2021.

n60d6caace76.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about types of hydroelectric plants?
o: A storage plant uses a dam to store water and regulate output
A run-of-the-river plant has little or no storage
A pumped-storage plant acts as a 'grid battery'
A run-of-the-river plant needs a large reservoir that substantially alters the watercourse
n60d6caace76.x: A run-of-the-river plant uses the natural flow with little or no storage and does not much alter the watercourse.

n5b776f275e0.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about dams in India?
o: India ranks second in the world in terms of large dams
About 98.5% of specified dams are owned by the States
Maharashtra has the most dams, followed by Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat
n5b776f275e0.x: India ranks third, not second, in the world in terms of large dams.

ndffaece6494.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about renewable energy in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Its current renewable-energy share is about 30%
It targets a renewable-energy share of more than 75% by 2047
Renewable energy already accounts for more than 75% of its share
Its target is associated with the Swarna Andhra Vision
ndffaece6494.x: Renewable energy is currently about 30% of the State's share; more than 75% is the 2047 target under the Swarna Andhra Vision.

nf1aecc8fdcf.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about flexible operation of the power system?
o: It includes cyclical operation of gas plants
It includes optimising hydro generation alongside coal
nf1aecc8fdcf.x: Batteries are one of the flexible-operation measures, along with pumped storage, cyclical gas operation and hydro optimisation.

n383d87f69d1.s:
Assertion (A): The Upper Sileru hydroelectric project has a capacity of 240 MW.
Reason (R): The Polavaram hydroelectric project has a capacity of 815.6 MW.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n383d87f69d1.x: Upper Sileru is 240 MW, but Polavaram has 960 MW, not 815.6 MW.

nc9d6749d71c.s:
Assertion (A): Window-I and Window-II of Revised SHAKTI do not use the same pricing mechanism.
Reason (R): Window-I gives coal at the notified price, whereas Window-II involves bidding at a premium.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nc9d6749d71c.x: The pricing differs precisely because Window-I uses the notified coal price while Window-II plants bid at a premium.

n7566dfc54d2.s:
Assertion (A): Only about 36% of India's hydroelectric potential has been developed.
Reason (R): India's small-hydro potential is estimated at 21,133 MW at 7,133 sites.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n7566dfc54d2.x: About 36% of the more than 145 GW potential is developed, and small-hydro potential is 21,133 MW at 7,133 sites, but R does not explain A.

nphysics-14-16.x: A solar cell turns light into electrical energy; a battery converts chemical, and a generator mechanical, energy into electrical energy.

nenvironment-32-4.s: The Appiko Movement is associated with:
nenvironment-32-4.x: Appiko is linked with Panduranga Hegde; Chipko with Gaura Devi, Narmada Bachao with Medha Patkar and Silent Valley with Salim Ali.

nphysics-14-58.s: Which of the following is NOT a form of potential energy?
nphysics-14-58.x: Thermal energy is internal energy from molecular motion; electric, chemical and nuclear energy are stored (potential) energy.

n39eaebc7d0a.s: Under India's dam safety framework, which body is the regulator and implements policy?
n39eaebc7d0a.x: NDSA is the regulator and implements policy; NCDS handles policy and standards and SCDS provides State oversight.

nphysics-14-34.s: A body in free fall converts:
nphysics-14-34.x: A falling body, like a swinging pendulum or a descending roller coaster, converts potential energy into kinetic energy.

nphysics-14-13.s: Mechanical energy is the sum of:
nphysics-14-13.x: Mechanical energy is KE + PE; thermal energy is internal energy due to molecular motion.

nenvironment-32-5.s: Who led the village women at Raini in 1974 during the Chipko Movement?
nenvironment-32-5.x: Gaura Devi led the women of Raini in 1974; Sunderlal Bahuguna was another leading Chipko figure.

n2775959e11e.s: In November 1999, the ceiling for small hydro projects under MNRE was raised to:
n2775959e11e.x: Small hydro up to 3 MW was transferred to MNRE in 1989 and the ceiling was raised to 25 MW in November 1999.

n8a389cc1347.s: The capacity of the Pinnapuram pumped-storage project, the world's first integrated renewable energy storage project, is:
n8a389cc1347.x: Pinnapuram in Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh, has a capacity of 1,680 MW.

ne62dd574548.s: The Srisailam hydroelectric project is situated on which river?
ne62dd574548.x: Srisailam is on the Krishna; its Right Bank Power House (770 MW) is in Andhra Pradesh and Left Bank Power House (900 MW) in Telangana.

n52f4e853cc9.s: In a hydroelectric power plant, energy is converted in the sequence:
n52f4e853cc9.x: Stored water's potential energy becomes kinetic energy as it falls, turns the turbine (mechanical) and the generator produces electricity.

n845c676b993.s: Large hydro projects (above 25 MW) are dealt with by:
n845c676b993.x: The Ministry of Power treats projects above 25 MW as large hydro, while MNRE handles small hydro up to 25 MW.

n6f70d1689f1.s: East-flowing peninsular rivers are generally more suited to:
n6f70d1689f1.x: East-flowing peninsular rivers are generally more suitable for irrigation, while waterfalls on peninsular rivers aid hydropower.

nenvironment-32-2.s: The Silent Valley Movement took place in which State?
nenvironment-32-2.x: The Silent Valley Movement was in Kerala; Chipko was in Uttarakhand and Appiko in Karnataka.

n126509d72a9.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Advanced Heavy Water Reactor (AHWR)?
o: It is a conceptual prototype designed at BARC
It is designed for large-scale use of plutonium-bearing spent fuel
It is regarded as India's flagship thorium reactor
It forms the core of the third stage of India's nuclear programme
n126509d72a9.x: The AHWR is intended for large-scale thorium use, not large-scale use of plutonium-bearing spent fuel.

n947949b62ff.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about radioactive series?
o: The uranium series begins with U-238 and ends with Pb-206
The thorium series begins with Th-232 and ends with Pb-208
The actinium series begins with U-235 and ends with Pb-207
The neptunium series is a natural radioactive series
n947949b62ff.x: The neptunium series is artificial, not natural.

ncbd6e52beac.s: Which of the following is wrongly matched?
o: Pu-239 – Fissile isotope produced from U-238 by neutron absorption
U-233 – Fissile fuel of Stage III and KAMINI
U-238 – Fissile fuel of Stage III and KAMINI
U-235 – Fissile isotope present in natural uranium
ncbd6e52beac.x: U-238 is the fertile isotope converted into Pu-239; the fuel of Stage III and KAMINI is U-233.

nf754f7d4c34.s: Which of the following research reactors is wrongly matched?
o: CIRUS – Natural uranium and heavy-water moderation
nf754f7d4c34.x: Dhruva is India's largest research reactor; Asia's first research reactor was APSARA.

n10a8285b442.s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
n10a8285b442.x: IGCAR is at Kalpakkam, where it works on FBR technology and its fuel cycle; AMD is the Hyderabad body.

n35fbfddaa97.s:
Assertion (A): NPCIL operates 25 reactors with an operating capacity of 8,880 MW.
Reason (R): India's nuclear capacity target is 22.38 GW by 2031–32.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n35fbfddaa97.x: Both figures are correct, but a future target does not explain the present fleet size.

ncd51fb7a94f.s:
Assertion (A): APSARA research reactor is located at Kalpakkam.
Reason (R): APSARA is a swimming-pool (pool-type) reactor.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
ncd51fb7a94f.x: APSARA is located at BARC, Trombay, not Kalpakkam; it is a pool-type reactor that became critical in 1956.

n60414659877.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: DAE and AEET both date to 1954)
n60414659877.s: AEET, set up in 1954, was renamed Bhabha Atomic Research Centre in:
n60414659877.x: BARC began in 1954 as AEET and was renamed in 1967 after Homi Bhabha.

n5e2c9ea0bb2.s: The Nuclear Energy Mission (Union Budget 2025-26) targets nuclear power capacity of ____ by 2047.
n5e2c9ea0bb2.x: The mission targets 100 GW by 2047, with Rs 20,000 crore for Small Modular Reactors.

ne5fa1425c5d.s: Xenon-135 is called a 'nuclear poison' because it:
ne5fa1425c5d.x: Xenon-135 absorbs neutrons and so acts as a nuclear poison in a reactor.

nb14835ce6c6.s: The coolant used in Stage II Fast Breeder Reactors of India is:
nb14835ce6c6.x: Stage II FBRs use liquid sodium coolant and no moderator, since fast neutrons are needed.

nc06bca7a28a.s: ANEEL fuel, developed by the US firm Clean Core Thorium Energy, combines thorium with:
nc06bca7a28a.x: ANEEL is thorium plus HALEU and can be used in existing PHWRs.

nbb7751c53fc.s: The CIRUS research reactor at Trombay was built in collaboration with:
nbb7751c53fc.x: CIRUS was built with Canada following a 1956 decision and was shut down in 2010.

nchemistry-11-23.s: A positively charged beta particle is a:
nchemistry-11-23.x: Positive beta is a positron; negative beta is an electron and an alpha particle is a +2 helium nucleus.

n366de7cf973.s: ITER is designed to give about 500 MW of output from an input of:
n366de7cf973.x: ITER, a tokamak fusion device, is designed for 500 MW output from 50 MW input, about ten times more out than in.

n05f3264f83d.s: The refuelling interval of Small Modular Reactors is about:
n05f3264f83d.x: SMRs are generally factory-built with a refuelling interval of about 3–7 years, longer than conventional reactors.

n29228e1b58d.s: In a fast breeder reactor, fast neutrons convert the U-238 blanket into:
n29228e1b58d.x: Fast neutrons turn the U-238 blanket into Pu-239, so the FBR breeds more fuel than it consumes.

nb4e98cb52a0.s: India possesses about what share of the world's thorium?
nb4e98cb52a0.x: India has about 25% of global thorium (and about 2% of uranium).

n4e7b90fe371.s: Which body is permitted to process and export monazite in India?
n4e7b90fe371.x: Only government bodies such as IREL may process and export monazite, found in the beach sands of Kerala and Odisha.

nd71b5ee1e66.s: All present-day nuclear electricity is generated through:
nd71b5ee1e66.x: Present-day reactors use fission; fusion occurs in the Sun and stars and fusion power is still at the R&D stage.

n4083ee763d0.s: Tritium is produced by bombarding ____ with neutrons.
n4083ee763d0.x: Tritium (1 proton + 2 neutrons) is produced by bombarding lithium with neutrons.

n43ba394209c.s: The Tummalapalle uranium mine of UCIL is located in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
n43ba394209c.x: Tummalapalle, a UCIL uranium mine with a processing plant, is in YSR Kadapa district.

nca9a4a0adfa.s: Stage I of India's three-stage nuclear programme is based on:
nca9a4a0adfa.x: Stage I uses PHWRs fuelled by natural uranium; its spent fuel yields Pu-239 for the next stage.

n74ed3e41254.s: The rated electrical capacity of the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam is:
n74ed3e41254.x: The sodium-cooled, pool-type PFBR is rated at 500 MWe (1,250 MWt).

n43c0cbaf0c4.s: India's tokamaks Aditya and SST-1 are located at:
n43c0cbaf0c4.x: Aditya (India's first tokamak) and SST-1 are at the Institute for Plasma Research, Gandhinagar, not BARC.

n25e76c3d91e.s: Compared with nuclear fission, nuclear fusion releases ____ energy per unit mass.
n25e76c3d91e.x: Fusion releases more energy per unit mass than fission, though it needs extremely high temperature and pressure.

nchemistry-11-18.s: ³H and ⁴He, each having two neutrons, are:
nchemistry-11-18.x: Nuclides with the same number of neutrons are isotones; ³H and ⁴He both have 2 neutrons.

nchemistry-11-4.s: Atoms having the same mass number but different atomic numbers are called:
nchemistry-11-4.x: Isobars share mass number but differ in atomic number; isotopes share atomic number but differ in mass number.

n281eab0c027.s: The splitting of a heavy nucleus is called:
n281eab0c027.x: Fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus, while fusion is the joining of two light nuclei.

n4a779b82ec6.s: In a hydrogen bomb, the fusion reaction is initiated by:
n4a779b82ec6.x: A hydrogen bomb uses fusion triggered by a fission explosion; an atomic bomb is based on uncontrolled fission.

n00464f9628b.s: The AHWR acts as a bridge between which stages of India's nuclear programme?
n00464f9628b.x: The AHWR bridges Stage I and Stage III, advancing thorium use without passing through Stage II.

ndisaster-management-7-13.s: Which of the following nuclear accidents is wrongly matched?
ndisaster-management-7-13.x: The Three Mile Island partial core meltdown in the USA occurred in 1979, not 1986.

n2ce59d9a2ed.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB)?
o: It licenses nuclear power plants and fuel-cycle facilities
It inspects facilities and can suspend or revoke licences
It does not regulate radiation safety in medical and industrial applications
It regulates management and transport of radioactive waste
n2ce59d9a2ed.x: The AERB does regulate radiation safety in medical and industrial applications, along with licensing, inspection and waste regulation.

n4ad2c6b7a64.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about milestones in India's nuclear power programme?
o: RAPS-1 was the first PHWR in India
MAPS was the first fully indigenous PHWR
Nangal housed the first Heavy Water Plant
KAPP-3 was the first PHWR in India
n4ad2c6b7a64.x: KAPP-3 was India's first 700 MW unit; the first PHWR was RAPS-1.

n86797fc3e2b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act (CLNDA), 2010?
o: Section 17(b) gave the operator a right of recourse against suppliers
The Indian Nuclear Insurance Pool was created to cover suppliers
It capped operator liability at Rs 1,500 crore
n86797fc3e2b.x: CLNDA made operator liability no-fault, capped at Rs 1,500 crore with the Centre paying beyond the cap.

n21a5a6fb9d4.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about firsts in India's nuclear power programme?
o: Tarapur went into operation in 1969 with two BWRs
Tarapur began operation in 1960 with two PHWRs
RAPS-1, the first PHWR, was built with AECL of Canada and started in 1972
Jaitapur, with a planned 9,900 MW, is the largest planned nuclear project
n21a5a6fb9d4.x: Tarapur, India's first nuclear power plant, started in 1969 with two boiling water reactors, not in 1960 with PHWRs.

n918a33d22fd.s:
Assertion (A): The AERB was set up on 15 November 1983 by an executive order under the Atomic Energy Act, 1962.
Reason (R): The Nuclear Safety Regulatory Authority Bill was enacted to give the AERB statutory status.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n918a33d22fd.x: The AERB was created by executive order in 1983, but the NSRA Bill was never enacted; statutory status came with the SHANTI Act, 2025.

n627feccf433.s:
Assertion (A): The Nuclear Security Summit series ended at Seoul.
Reason (R): India announced the Global Centre for Nuclear Energy Partnership at the 2010 summit.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n627feccf433.x: The four summits (Washington 2010, Seoul 2012, The Hague 2014, Washington 2016) ended at Washington; India did announce GCNEP, now at Bahadurgarh, in 2010.

ndisaster-management-7-7.s:
Assertion (A): Chernobyl and Fukushima Daiichi were both rated Level 7 on the INES.
Reason (R): The Mayapuri radiological incident occurred in Delhi in 2010.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
ndisaster-management-7-7.x: Both statements are true, but the Mayapuri incident has no bearing on the INES rating of Chernobyl and Fukushima.

n2e657c939f4.s: The SHANTI Act, 2025 caps total nuclear liability at:
n2e657c939f4.x: Total liability is capped at 300 million SDR (about Rs 3,900 crore); the excess is met through a Nuclear Liability Fund.

nff478b074cd.s: India signed its civil nuclear agreement with Japan in:
nff478b074cd.x: The India-Japan civil nuclear agreement dates to 2016; France's was of 30 September 2008 and Australia's of 2014.

n3b7830da309.s: The India-US 123 Agreement is named after Section 123 of the:
n3b7830da309.x: The name comes from Section 123 of the US Atomic Energy Act, 1954; the agreement was signed under Manmohan Singh and George W. Bush.

n58b2d895670.s: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), founded in 1957, is headquartered at:
n58b2d895670.x: The IAEA is headquartered at Vienna, Austria; India is a founding member.

n71847c0c613.s: The Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW) entered into force in:
n71847c0c613.x: The TPNW entered into force in 2021; India has not signed it, holding that it adds nothing to customary law.

n8eaa7588256.s: The Convention on Nuclear Safety, adopted in 1994, entered into force in:
n8eaa7588256.x: The Convention was adopted in 1994 and came into force in 1996; India is a party to it.

n878f2916b9e.s: Besides civil-society protests, which event delayed the Kudankulam nuclear project?
o: The signing of the India-US 123 Agreement
n878f2916b9e.x: The breakup of the USSR and civil-society protests are counted among the delays; the 1991 economic crisis is not.

ne2fd2a3dbbb.s: Thal is located in which State?
ne2fd2a3dbbb.x: Thal is in Maharashtra, not Gujarat; Nangal is in Punjab and Talcher in Odisha.

nd4d5f81d13c.s: Along with the Atomic Energy Act, 1962, the SHANTI Act, 2025 repealed the:
o: Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010
nd4d5f81d13c.x: The SHANTI Act repealed the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the CLNDA, 2010; it only amended Section 4 of the Patents Act.

ne7bd958a8c9.s: Under the SHANTI Act, 2025, the Government retains control over:
o: Spent-fuel reprocessing and heavy-water production only
Enrichment, spent-fuel reprocessing and heavy-water production
ne7bd958a8c9.x: The Government retains control over all three: enrichment, spent-fuel reprocessing and heavy-water production.

n429f3e40cc1.s: KAPP-3, India's first indigenous 700 MW PHWR, is located in:
n429f3e40cc1.x: KAPP-3 is at Kakrapar in Gujarat and began commercial operation on 30 June 2023.

n5d7b2259c43.s: The Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG), which takes decisions by consensus, has how many members?
n5d7b2259c43.x: The NSG has 48 members, works by consensus and has no permanent secretariat.

nd88905c6139.s: India's Additional Protocol with the IAEA, signed in 2009, came into force in:
nd88905c6139.x: India signed the Additional Protocol in 2009 and it came into force in 2014; it covers only declared civilian facilities.

nf6acb2c540b.s: Caesium-137 and ____, from medical or industrial sources, are typical materials for a dirty bomb.
nf6acb2c540b.x: Caesium-137 and Cobalt-60 are the typical dirty-bomb materials; U-235 in a reactor core is not included.

n41a0f019ad5.s: Under the SHANTI Act, 2025, the liability cap for small modular reactors is:
n41a0f019ad5.x: The graded caps are ₹3,000 crore for large facilities, ₹1,500 crore for medium facilities and ₹100 crore for SMRs.

nc8d6a305fb6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about radiometric dating?
o: U-238 to Pb-206 dating is used for the oldest rocks and the age of the Earth
Carbon-14 dating is used mainly for volcanic rocks older than a billion years
K-40 to Ar-40 dating is used for volcanic rocks and fossil-bearing layers
Carbon-14 dating covers once-living remains up to about 50,000 years
nc8d6a305fb6.x: Carbon-14 (half-life about 5,730 years) dates once-living organic remains up to about 50,000 years, not ancient volcanic rocks.

n7f7d3b30680.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about food irradiation in India?
o: Irradiated mangoes have been exported to the United States
Irradiation can be carried out on packed food
Irradiation cannot be applied to bulk food
n7f7d3b30680.x: Irradiation can be carried out on packed or bulk food.

naf4561a0fde.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about industrial uses of radiotracers?
o: Sediment tracking at ports increases the frequency of desilting campaigns
They detect leaks in buried oil and gas pipelines
They are used to study seepage from dams
They are used for flow measurement
naf4561a0fde.x: Radiotracer tracking of sediment transport can help reduce, not increase, the frequency of desilting campaigns.

n7e21333ae38.s:
Assertion (A): A radioisotope thermoelectric generator (RTG) has no moving parts.
Reason (R): An RTG converts heat from radioactive decay into electricity through thermocouples based on the Seebeck effect.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n7e21333ae38.x: An RTG is not a fission reactor; it converts decay heat directly into electricity with thermocouples (Seebeck effect), so it needs no moving parts.

n5ec07b66778.s:
Assertion (A): Nuclear moisture gauges help determine irrigation requirements.
Reason (R): BARC applies tissue culture to propagate banana and pineapple.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n5ec07b66778.x: Both are true agricultural applications of nuclear techniques, but tissue culture does not explain moisture gauging.

n73612d6dc52.s: The most widely used diagnostic radioisotope is:
n73612d6dc52.x: Technetium-99m is the most widely used diagnostic isotope, used to image the heart, brain, bones and lungs.

nf8780b565d5.s: India's leading producer of radioisotopes is:
nf8780b565d5.x: BARC, set up as AEET in 1954 and renamed in 1967, is India's leading producer of radioisotopes.

n27c5ad26cc8.s: The largest research reactor of BARC is:
n27c5ad26cc8.x: Dhruva is the largest research reactor; Apsara was Asia's first and KAMINI is the only U-233-fuelled reactor.

na5657f0dead.s:
Assertion (A): India achieved 50% non-fossil installed capacity in June 2025, five years ahead of schedule.
Reason (R): The 2015 NDC had set a target of 40% non-fossil capacity by 2030.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
na5657f0dead.x: Both are true, but the 2015 40% target does not explain achieving the later 50% target (set by the updated NDC and COP26 Panchamrit).

n45e3ca51a2c.s: In 2024–25, renewable energy contributed about ____ of India's electricity generation.
n45e3ca51a2c.x: Renewables were about half of installed capacity but supplied only about 22% of generation; coal and thermal gave about 75%.

n25680833317.s: Which of the following is a conventional source of energy?
n25680833317.x: Firewood is a conventional source; solar energy is non-conventional and wind energy renewable.

ne574b477524.s: Which of the following is a renewable resource?
ne574b477524.x: Geothermal energy, like wind, is renewable; coal and nuclear fuels are finite, non-renewable resources.

n2b61c607aef.s: Which of the following is NOT a source of green energy?
n2b61c607aef.x: Natural gas is a fossil fuel; sunlight, wind and algae-based sources are green.

n35ebe0c6cb8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about solar thermal (concentrated solar power) technology?
o: Mirrors may concentrate sunlight to heat a fluid
Heat storage is not possible in such systems
The heat can produce steam for a turbine
Solar power towers are associated with solar thermal applications
n35ebe0c6cb8.x: Solar thermal systems can store heat; they collect or concentrate solar heat for water, steam and power generation.

na086ca458ac.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Andhra Pradesh's solar-energy cluster?
o: Kurnool and YSR Kadapa parks anchor the Rayalaseema renewable-energy cluster
NTPC Simhadri has a floating solar plant in Visakhapatnam
SECI is the State nodal agency
About 50,000 acres of barren land have been offered for solar lease
na086ca458ac.x: NEDCAP, not SECI, is the nodal agency for Andhra Pradesh's solar programme.

na8885e9218b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana?
o: It provides free power up to 500 units per month
It is a Central Sector scheme for 2024 to 2026-27
It aims to cover one crore rooftop households
It envisages 30 GW of rooftop solar capacity
na8885e9218b.x: The scheme provides free power up to 300 units per month, not 500.

nenvironment-1-6.s:
Assertion (A): Seshachalam is the first Biosphere Reserve of Andhra Pradesh.
Reason (R): Surat was the first district with 100% solar-powered primary health centres.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nenvironment-1-6.x: Both statements are true, but they are unrelated, so R does not explain A.

neecddaf1cb6.s:
Assertion (A): ALMM applies only to projects implemented by private developers.
Reason (R): Only ALMM-listed modules may be used in government-funded, open-access and net-metering projects.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
neecddaf1cb6.x: ALMM (compulsory since 2019) also covers government-funded and government-linked projects such as PM Surya Ghar, PM-KUSUM and SECI tenders, so A is false.

n77c4ccc9f63.s:
Assertion (A): In June 2015, the National Solar Mission's grid-connected target was revised from 20 GW to 100 GW by 2022.
Reason (R): The revised 100 GW target comprised 60 GW of rooftop solar and 40 GW of large/medium projects.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n77c4ccc9f63.x: The target was revised to 100 GW in June 2015, but the split was 40 GW rooftop and 60 GW large/medium, not the reverse.

n08e4deedadf.s: Compared with land-based installations, the upfront cost of floating solar projects is approximately:
n08e4deedadf.x: Floating solar costs about 25% more upfront, but saves land, reduces evaporation and gains efficiency from water cooling.

n5dbe7fa9611.s: Which State leads India's floating solar potential on reservoirs, with about 16 GW?
n5dbe7fa9611.x: Maharashtra (about 16 GW) and Madhya Pradesh (about 14 GW) lead the national potential of about 102.18 GW.

naab9341f614.s: India's solar capacity addition in 2025, which beat that of the US for the first time, was about:
naab9341f614.x: India added about 38 GW in 2025, becoming the second-largest solar growth market and overtaking the US for the first time.

ne665da0ccc9.s: Most parts of India receive solar irradiation of about ____ per square metre per day.
ne665da0ccc9.x: Most of India receives 4–7 kWh/m²/day, with 250–300 clear sunny days a year.

ncd2dbbf786b.s: The ALMM module list covers approximately ____ of manufacturing capacity.
ncd2dbbf786b.x: The module list covers about 190 GW, while the cell list covers only about 25 GW.

n9acc53d7baa.s: On 21 March 2017, the target of the Solar Park Scheme was enhanced to:
n9acc53d7baa.x: Launched on 12 December 2014 with a 20 GW target for over 25 parks, the scheme was raised to 40 GW on 21 March 2017.

o: Small grid-connected plants on barren land or farmland
n78d3b581f5c.x: Component B covers standalone solar pumps; A covers small grid-connected plants and C solarisation of grid-connected pumps.

nc3df6fa53ce.s: The Indian Energy Exchange (IEX), established in 2008, is regulated by:
nc3df6fa53ce.x: IEX is regulated by CERC and trades DAM, TAM, renewable energy and ESCerts.

na663321501e.s: The outlay of PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana is about:
na663321501e.x: The scheme, launched in February 2024, has an outlay of about Rs 75,021 crore.

nda92b474023.s: The Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission ('Solar India') was launched in:
nda92b474023.x: The mission was launched in January 2010 as one of NAPCC's eight missions; June 2015 is when its target was revised to 100 GW.

n939e54a8e6d.s: Which of the following is reported to be still absent in India's solar sector?
o: An approved list of module manufacturers (ALMM)
n939e54a8e6d.x: Solar-waste recycling norms are still absent; cell capacity lag and grid curtailment are other concerns.

nenvironment-1-4.s: The first World Climate Conference was held in:
nenvironment-1-4.x: The first World Climate Conference was in 1979; the first Earth Summit was at Rio in 1992.

nc352c6d6636.s: ALMM List-III for ingots and wafers becomes mandatory from:
nc352c6d6636.x: List-III becomes mandatory only from June 2028; List-II for cells (ALCM) applies from 1 June 2026.

ne10f15af291.s: NISE has estimated India's ground-based solar potential, assuming use of 3% of wasteland, at about:
ne10f15af291.x: NISE estimates about 748 GW, of which only about 4.5% has been used.

nenvironment-1-5.s: The world's first fully solar-powered airport is:
nenvironment-1-5.x: Cochin International Airport is the world's first fully solar-powered airport.

n932a3c18527.s: The Green Energy Open Access Rules, 2022 cut the open-access threshold for green power from 1 MW to:
n932a3c18527.x: The Ministry of Power's Rules cut the threshold from 1 MW to 100 kW.

n3944801f431.s: India's reported installed solar capacity, about 29 per cent of total capacity, is:
n3944801f431.x: Reported installed solar capacity was 157.05 GW, about 29 per cent of total capacity.

na7b0b13d4b2.s: The State nodal agency for solar development in Andhra Pradesh is:
na7b0b13d4b2.x: NEDCAP is the State nodal agency for Andhra Pradesh's solar programme; SECI and MNRE have national-level roles.

n14777861be3.s: The dominant solar-cell technology in the market is:
n14777861be3.x: Crystalline silicon (mono- and polycrystalline) cells dominate the market; thin-film cells are cheaper and flexible but less efficient.

n6c83bff1a23.s: The National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE), an autonomous body of MNRE, is located at:
n6c83bff1a23.x: NISE is at Gurugram and is the technical focal point for solar R&D.

ne61684c9566.s: The Omkareshwar floating solar project (278 MW) is located on which river?
ne61684c9566.x: Omkareshwar floating solar is on the Narmada in Khandwa district, Madhya Pradesh, and is planned to reach 600 MW.

n159f2fa2e1f.x: ALMM List-I covers modules, List-II cells and List-III ingots and wafers.

n871d6820de9.s: The stated capacity-utilisation factor of solar power in India is about:
n871d6820de9.x: The stated CUFs are about 21% for solar, 36–40% for wind and about 85% for coal.

n87c42ace21b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE)?
o: It prepares the Indian Wind Atlas
It is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Power
It supports testing and certification of wind technologies
It undertakes wind-resource assessment and site identification
n87c42ace21b.x: NIWE is an autonomous body under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, not the Ministry of Power.

nddd9a588548.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's installed wind-power capacity?
o: It first crossed 50 GW in March 2014
nddd9a588548.x: Capacity was only 21.04 GW in March 2014; it crossed 50 GW in March 2025.

n75150a540f5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Green Energy Corridor (GEC)?
o: It has been under way since 2015
Andhra Pradesh is among the 8 States of Intra-State GEC-I
Odisha is among the 8 States of Intra-State GEC-I
Tamil Nadu is among the 8 States of Intra-State GEC-I
n75150a540f5.x: Intra-State GEC-I covers AP, Gujarat, HP, Karnataka, MP, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu; Odisha is not among them.

n82baff55349.s:
Assertion (A): The offshore wind Viability Gap Funding scheme provides 500 MW each off Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.
Reason (R): The scheme was approved in 2024.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n82baff55349.x: The 2024 scheme covers the first 1 GW, split equally between Gujarat and Tamil Nadu, but its approval year does not explain the split.

nd3068e09525.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Vertical-axis wind turbine – Higher efficiency than a horizontal-axis turbine
Horizontal-axis wind turbine – Rotor axis parallel to the wind
Horizontal-axis wind turbine – No yaw control needed
nd3068e09525.x: A HAWT has its rotor axis parallel to the wind and needs yaw control; VAWTs such as Darrieus and Savonius take wind from any direction but have lower efficiency.

n855c3a1049c.s: The nodal agency under the National Offshore Wind Energy Policy, 2015 is:
n855c3a1049c.x: MNRE is the nodal ministry and NIWE, not SECI, is the nodal agency for offshore wind farms in India's EEZ.

n9640945f6cb.s: Which country ranks second in the world in installed wind-power capacity?
n9640945f6cb.x: The top three are China, the United States of America and Germany, in that order.

ne3a90655653.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about biogas?
o: Methane makes up about 85–95% of biogas
It is mainly methane and CO2 from anaerobic digestion of organic matter
Its methane is formed by methanogenic archaea in the absence of oxygen
The slurry left after digestion is a good organic manure
ne3a90655653.x: Methane is about 50–75% of biogas; 85–95% is the methane share of piped natural gas.

n42174f65551.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about MNRE's classification of energy sources?
o: Bio-power includes biomass, bagasse cogeneration and waste-to-energy
Geothermal, tidal and OTEC are renewable sources under development
Nuclear power is classified as renewable energy
Nuclear capacity of 8.78 GW is counted separately
n42174f65551.x: Nuclear power is non-fossil but not classified as renewable; its capacity is counted separately.

naa2a5067617.s: Which of the following waste-to-energy routes is wrongly matched?
o: Incineration – Direct burning of municipal solid waste
Refuse-derived fuel – Dry combustible part of segregated MSW
naa2a5067617.x: Pyrolysis is heating without oxygen; partial oxidation is gasification.

n64ff25a4f9e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2022 amendment to the National Policy on Biofuels?
o: It permitted biofuel units in SEZs and EOUs under Make in India
It permitted exports in specific cases
It barred the addition of new members to the NBCC
n64ff25a4f9e.x: The amendment allowed new members to be added to the NBCC.

n76d3f6c92c1.s: Which of the following 2G ethanol plants is wrongly matched?
n76d3f6c92c1.x: HPCL Bathinda is in Punjab; Bargarh is the Odisha plant.

n6753089fbb7.s:
Assertion (A): The National Policy on Biofuels, 2018 widened the ethanol feedstock base beyond molasses.
Reason (R): It included sugarcane juice, surplus FCI rice, maize and damaged foodgrains as ethanol feedstocks.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n6753089fbb7.x: The base widened beyond molasses precisely because these new feedstocks were included.

n2091b28d515.s: Which section of the Motor Vehicles Act permits engine conversion to biofuels?
n2091b28d515.x: Section 52 of the Motor Vehicles Act permits conversion of engines to biofuels.

ncf45919cd06.s: India's Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) target for international flights by 2030 is:
ncf45919cd06.x: The SAF roadmap sets 1% by 2027, 2% by 2028 and 5% by 2030, in line with ICAO's net-zero 2050 goal.

n996bf8f7cef.s: The 2022 amendment to the National Policy on Biofuels advanced the E20 target to Ethanol Supply Year:
n996bf8f7cef.x: The 2018 policy aimed at E20 by 2030; the 2022 amendment advanced it to ESY 2025-26.

n680efd77a49.s: In the food-versus-fuel debate, the rise in maize area has been accompanied by a decline in the area under:
n680efd77a49.x: Maize-ethanol pricing has been linked with diversion of land from pulses and oilseeds.

nf9a90936983.s: About 94% of India's biodiesel feedstock is:
nf9a90936983.x: Palm stearin oil accounts for about 94% of India's biodiesel feedstock.

na32b7d7b643.s: Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion (OTEC) needs a temperature difference between surface and deep water of about:
na32b7d7b643.x: OTEC needs about a 20°C difference and is viable mainly between 30°N and 30°S.

nbf2012e6644.s: The Ministry of Power policy of 2021 mandated biomass co-firing in coal-based plants at:
nbf2012e6644.x: The 2021 policy mandated 5% biomass co-firing in coal plants, to rise to 7%.

nee0ac5ae0c6.s: India's first commercial-scale bamboo bioethanol plant, dedicated on 14 September 2025, is at:
nee0ac5ae0c6.x: The Numaligarh plant uses bamboo, a non-food lignocellulosic (second-generation) feedstock.

n6df1b12147b.s: India's first geothermal power project, led by ONGC, is at:
n6df1b12147b.x: India's first geothermal project is at Puga Valley, Ladakh, led by ONGC.

n9d8b1a63eb1.s: Which of the following is identified as an OTEC location in India?
n9d8b1a63eb1.x: Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are OTEC locations; the Gulfs of Khambhat and Kutch are tidal-energy sites.

nb50f6f2aa71.s: India's National Policy on Geothermal Energy (2025) provides for how many pilot projects?
nb50f6f2aa71.x: The policy, notified by MNRE on 15 September 2025, has five pilot projects, not ten.

n4c50f34467f.s: The Surajkund geothermal field is located in:
n4c50f34467f.x: Surajkund geothermal field is in Jharkhand; Tapovan is in Uttarakhand and Puga Valley in Ladakh.

na24c0629784.s: GOBARdhan (Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan) was launched in:
na24c0629784.x: GOBARdhan was launched in 2018, the same year as SATAT.

n46f16323f10.s: India's target for biodiesel blending in diesel by 2030 is:
n46f16323f10.x: India targets 5% biodiesel blending by 2030; actual blending remains below 0.5%.

nf94afd10989.s: The Phase-I outlay of the National Bioenergy Programme (2021–2026) is:
nf94afd10989.x: Phase-I (1 April 2021 to 31 March 2026) has an outlay of ₹858 crore, implemented by MNRE through State Nodal Agencies.

nc63beac3a99.s: Mini hydro plants are those with a capacity of:
o: Above 2 MW and up to 25 MW
nc63beac3a99.x: Micro hydro is up to 100 kW, mini hydro 101 kW to 2 MW and small hydro above 2 MW up to 25 MW.

n011a7c19f22.s: Mandatory E20 ethanol-blended petrol is scheduled from:
n011a7c19f22.x: Mandatory E20 is scheduled from 1 April 2026; BIS standards extend up to E30.

nfad2c96fea9.s: The implementation timeline of the revised PM JI-VAN Yojana extends to:
nfad2c96fea9.x: The revised scheme covers advanced biofuels, including bolt-on and brownfield projects, up to 2028–29.

n0994c9bee63.s: Which of the following is a limitation of algal biofuel?
n0994c9bee63.x: Energy-intensive lipid extraction is a limitation; high yield and use of wastewater and CO2 are advantages.

n0aaaed0f04e.s: Small hydro projects are commonly developed at:
o: Hill streams and canal falls only
Canal falls and toes of dams only
Hill streams, canal falls and toes of dams
n0aaaed0f04e.x: Run-of-river small hydro may use hill streams, canal falls and water released at dam toes.

ndc207dd2f72.s: Hot springs, geysers and volcanoes are surface expressions of:
ndc207dd2f72.x: They are surface expressions of heat originating within the Earth, i.e. geothermal energy.

n7327d8e1c7f.s: The 'Gramalakshmi' floating-drum gobar gas plant of Jashbhai Patel was popularised by:
n7327d8e1c7f.x: The 1950s Gramalakshmi plant was popularised by KVIC, not MNRE.

nenvironment-36-9.s: Producer gas (synthetic gas) is a mixture of carbon monoxide, hydrogen, carbon dioxide and:
nenvironment-36-9.x: Producer gas is a mix of CO, H₂, CO₂ and methane.

na899bac848c.s: India achieved E10 ethanol blending in petrol in:
na899bac848c.x: After the 2001 pilot and E5 from 1 January 2003, E10 was achieved in June 2022; E20 is mandatory from 1 April 2026.

n6a335d7acad.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about applications of green hydrogen in India?
o: It is not being considered for steel
Fuel-cell trucks, buses and ships are potential applications
Hydrogen blending in city-gas networks is being evaluated as H-CNG
Long-duration energy storage is a potential application
n6a335d7acad.x: Green hydrogen is being considered for fertilisers, refineries and steel.

n6579a053a22.s:
Assertion (A): PEM electrolysers are suited to variable renewable energy.
Reason (R): A PEM electrolyser uses a solid polymer membrane that responds quickly to variable renewable energy.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n6579a053a22.x: PEM's quick response, via its solid polymer membrane, is what makes it suited to variable renewable energy.

nchemistry-10-7.s: Methane pyrolysis (natural gas heated without oxygen) produces which type of hydrogen?
nchemistry-10-7.x: Methane pyrolysis gives turquoise hydrogen; steam methane reforming gives grey or blue and renewable electrolysis green.

nbea63a00d55.s: The National Green Hydrogen Mission is expected to create about ____ jobs by 2030.
nbea63a00d55.x: The Mission expects about 6 lakh jobs, over ₹8 lakh crore investment and about 50 MMT annual GHG reduction.

n86757ebbc6c.s: In a PEM fuel cell, hydrogen is split into protons and electrons at the:
n86757ebbc6c.x: Hydrogen splits at the anode; protons cross the membrane to the cathode and electrons flow through the external circuit.

nchemistry-10-2.x: Blue hydrogen captures CO₂ for low emissions; grey releases it, green has zero and brown/black very high emissions.

nchemistry-10-18.s: In the steel sector, hydrogen helps decarbonise production through:
o: Direct reduced iron replacing coking coal
nchemistry-10-18.x: Steel uses hydrogen-based direct reduced iron in place of coking coal.

ndf5954de62e.s: Hydrogen that occurs naturally through geological processes is called:
ndf5954de62e.x: White hydrogen is naturally occurring geological hydrogen.

n53fcbc9df99.s: SHIP under the National Green Hydrogen Mission stands for:
n53fcbc9df99.x: SHIP is the Strategic Hydrogen Innovation Partnership, a PPP for R&D.

n511d1b65af6.s: The Green Hydrogen Valley Declaration of Andhra Pradesh (19 July 2025) was made at:
n511d1b65af6.x: The declaration was made at Amaravati to make AP India's green hydrogen capital.

n16b960f5146.s: Pink hydrogen is produced by electrolysis using:
n16b960f5146.x: Pink hydrogen comes from electrolysis powered by nuclear energy.

ncc491122791.s: V.O. Chidambaranar Port, which has a ₹35 crore green hydrogen bunkering pilot, is in:
ncc491122791.x: V.O. Chidambaranar Port is in Tamil Nadu, not Odisha.

n2dd0dc87a43.s: India's national net-zero target year is:
n2dd0dc87a43.x: India's net-zero target is 2070; 2047 is linked with energy independence.

nchemistry-10-8.s: Which of the following is an industrial, not a fuel or transport, use of hydrogen?
nchemistry-10-8.x: Ammonia for fertiliser is an industrial use; fuel-cell vehicles, rocket fuel and CNG blending are fuel uses.

n37979f74d70.s: The nodal ministry of the National Green Hydrogen Mission is:
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
n37979f74d70.x: MNRE is the nodal ministry; BEE under the Ministry of Power handles only certification.

nchemistry-10-6.s: Hydrogen produced from natural gas with carbon capture and storage is called:
nchemistry-10-6.x: That is blue hydrogen; green hydrogen comes from electrolysis using renewable power.

nchemistry-10-5.s: A fuel cell produces electricity and ____ from hydrogen and oxygen.
nchemistry-10-5.x: A fuel cell converts hydrogen and oxygen electrochemically into electricity and water, with zero emissions at the point of use.

n3c4e6c0171a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Extended Producer Responsibility under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022?
o: Producers, including importers, must collect waste batteries
Producers may dispose of collected waste batteries in landfills
Producers must recycle or refurbish waste batteries
Producers must use recycled material in new batteries
n3c4e6c0171a.x: Landfill disposal of waste batteries is prohibited.

n7c3ba733eb7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about storage for renewable-energy integration in India?
o: CEA estimated a requirement of 336 GWh of storage by 2029–30
India had about 500 MWh of BESS capacity in September 2025
Existing BESS capacity is far below the estimated requirement
Existing BESS capacity equals the estimated requirement
n7c3ba733eb7.x: The requirement is 336 GWh against about 500 MWh of existing BESS, so they are not equal.

n202c091dd23.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Battery Pack Aadhaar (BPAN)?
o: It is mandatory for portable batteries of every capacity
It is mandatory for electric vehicle batteries
It is mandatory for industrial batteries exceeding 2 kWh
It does not cover all household electrical appliances
n202c091dd23.x: BPAN is mandatory only for EV batteries and industrial batteries above 2 kWh, not every portable battery.

n673f58e69e4.s:
Assertion (A): The Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 were notified by MoEFCC, replacing the Batteries (Management and Handling) Rules, 2001.
Reason (R): The 2022 Rules permit incineration of waste batteries.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n673f58e69e4.x: The Rules were notified by MoEFCC and replaced the 2001 Rules, but they ban both landfill disposal and incineration.

n72e53a2ebe3.s:
Assertion (A): Graphite is generally the anode material of a lithium-ion battery.
Reason (R): Lithium, nickel and cobalt are usually used in the cathode of a lithium-ion battery.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n72e53a2ebe3.x: Both are true, but the cathode's composition does not explain why graphite is the anode.

n5e6f20abc58.s: The National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage is run by the:
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
n5e6f20abc58.x: The ACC programme (approved 12 May 2021, 50 GWh, Rs 18,100 crore) is run by the Ministry of Heavy Industries.

n09fd131ac05.s: In a battery, the electrolyte permits the movement of ____ between the electrodes.
n09fd131ac05.x: An electrolyte lets ions flow and keeps the electrodes apart; it does not provide a direct electronic path.

naa3dab64718.s: India's stated goal for EV penetration by 2030 is:
naa3dab64718.x: The goal is 30 percent EV penetration by 2030, against about 8.5 percent with over 25 lakh registrations in FY 2025-26.

ne0a525ad94b.s: Which of the following are policy measures for battery energy storage systems (BESS) in India?
o: Waiver of ISTS charges for co-located storage only
Consumer ownership or leasing of storage only
Recognition of storage as a power-system element only
ne0a525ad94b.x: All three are stated measures: ISTS waiver for co-located storage, consumer ownership or leasing, and recognition of ESS as a power-system element.

n71fbb61fe47.s: A vehicle that combines an engine with a battery-motor system and can be plugged in for charging is a:
n71fbb61fe47.x: A PHEV is a hybrid that can be charged externally; a plain HEV combines engine and battery-motor but is not plugged in.

n6efbfb61164.s: The outlay of the National Critical Mineral Mission, approved in 2025, is:
n6efbfb61164.x: The Mission's outlay is Rs 16,300 crore; its recycling incentive scheme is Rs 1,500 crore.

n3e3277f1d84.s: The use of nickel-cadmium batteries has declined partly because of the toxicity of:
n3e3277f1d84.x: Ni-Cd batteries are rechargeable but have become less common because cadmium is toxic.

n8d8f62db187.s: India's battery swapping policy was announced in the Union Budget of:
n8d8f62db187.x: The battery swapping policy was announced in Budget 2022-23; PM E-DRIVE replaced FAME-II in 2024.

n02f8372dd53.s: FCEV, an alternative powertrain vehicle, stands for:
n02f8372dd53.x: FCEV is a Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle; BEVs and fuel cell-electric hybrids are also alternative powertrain vehicles.

nf19e8a6478b.s: During the discharge of an electrochemical cell, oxidation occurs at the:
nf19e8a6478b.x: Oxidation (loss of electrons) occurs at the anode and reduction (gain of electrons) at the cathode.

nb24d707def1.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about fuel-efficiency and conservation initiatives?
o: CAFE norms set average fuel-efficiency targets for M1 cars
The first CAFE norms were notified in 2017
SAKSHAM is a fuel-conservation drive of the Bureau of Energy Efficiency
The Bureau of Energy Efficiency enforces the CAFE norms
nb24d707def1.x: SAKSHAM is conducted by the Petroleum Conservation Research Association (PCRA), not BEE.

n677a4c29d88.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the UK Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) and India?
o: In September 2026 the UK recognised India's CCTS as a qualifying carbon price
The UK CBAM applies from 1 January 2026
The UK CBAM covers aluminium and cement
The UK CBAM covers fertiliser, hydrogen, and iron and steel
n677a4c29d88.x: The UK CBAM applies from 1 January 2027, not 2026.

n01c98df3ba5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the State Energy Efficiency Index (SEEI)?
o: It was developed by BEE with the Alliance for an Energy Efficient Economy
It forms the basis for the National Energy Conservation Awards
Front Runner is one of its categories
It classifies States into only three categories
n01c98df3ba5.x: SEEI uses four categories: Front Runner, Achiever, Contender and Aspirant.

nc31ee53a815.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the 2022 amendment to the Energy Conservation Act?
o: It kept large residential buildings outside energy-conservation codes
Designated consumers must use a minimum share of non-fossil energy
Efficiency norms may be prescribed for vehicles
Efficiency norms may be prescribed for vessels
nc31ee53a815.x: The amendment brought large residential buildings under energy-conservation codes.

n110ef057cb9.s:
Assertion (A): National Energy Conservation Day is observed on 14 December.
Reason (R): The National Energy Conservation Awards are given annually by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n110ef057cb9.x: The Day is 14 December, but NECA (instituted 1991) is given by BEE under the Ministry of Power, not MNRE.

n2e9ac5ca5d4.s:
Assertion (A): The Energy Conservation Act, 2001 provides penalties for non-compliance.
Reason (R): The Act provides for energy audits of designated consumers.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n2e9ac5ca5d4.x: Both are provisions of the Act, but providing for audits does not explain the existence of penalties.

n8975b1fe2ba.s: Under BEE's Standards and Labelling programme, each additional star saves approximately:
n8975b1fe2ba.x: The one-to-five-star programme (over 40 equipment types) saves about 10–15 per cent energy per additional star.

n1bad6874f7e.s: Energy Saving Certificates (ESCerts) under the PAT scheme are traded on:
n1bad6874f7e.x: Over-achievers earn ESCerts and under-achievers buy them on power exchanges, including the Indian Energy Exchange.

n439726be949.s: ECO Niwas Samhita, introduced in 2018, is an energy code for:
n439726be949.x: ECO Niwas Samhita (2018) covers residential buildings; ECBC (2007) covers new commercial buildings.

n947c4848f62.s: India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, notified in 2023, is provided for under:
n947c4848f62.x: Section 14AA provides for the CCTS, India's first mandatory compliance carbon market.

ne2b7bf35732.s: The National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency is one of how many missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change?
ne2b7bf35732.x: NMEEE is one of the eight missions under NAPCC (2008).

n7280eb7d3d7.s: The regulator of India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme is:
n7280eb7d3d7.x: CERC is the regulator, while BEE is the administrator of the scheme.

nc0f25fc1634.s: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency, a statutory body created by the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, functions under the:
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
nc0f25fc1634.x: BEE functions under the Ministry of Power; the JV of power PSUs that distributes LEDs is EESL.

nd217f6b6444.s: Energy efficiency strengthens energy security in India, which depends on imports for about ____ of its oil.
nd217f6b6444.x: India imports about 80% of its oil, so cheap demand reduction through efficiency improves energy security.

n4aeca84f6d6.s: Which of the following scheme–ministry pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (2016) – Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (2024) – MNRE
n4aeca84f6d6.x: PM-KUSUM was launched by MNRE, not the Ministry of Power (which runs UDAY).

nf731b69b7d2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about UDAY?
o: States took over 75% of DISCOM debt outstanding as on 30 September 2015
50% of the debt was taken over in 2015-16
The arrangement covered only half of total outstanding DISCOM debt
25% of the debt was taken over in 2016-17
nf731b69b7d2.x: The arrangement covered 97% of total outstanding DISCOM debt.

nb9a28eda080.s:
Assertion (A): The Grameen Vitrak Yojana (2009) raised the rural share of LPG distributors from 18% to 60%.
Reason (R): Surya Nutan, an indoor solar stove launched in 2022, was developed by EESL.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nb9a28eda080.x: A is correct, but Surya Nutan was developed by IOCL, not EESL.

nb0984ff3bc5.s: UDAY targeted a reduction of AT&C losses to ____ by 2018-19.
nb0984ff3bc5.x: UDAY targeted AT&C losses of 15% and a zero ACS-ARR gap by 2018-19.

nd690bb69e0e.s: Under PM Surya Ghar, Central Financial Assistance covers ____ of the cost for the first 2 kW.
nd690bb69e0e.x: CFA covers 60% of the cost for 2 kW and 40% for additional capacity up to 3 kW.

n5372decc0e0.s: As per the latest figure, how many willing households were electrified under Saubhagya?
n5372decc0e0.x: Saubhagya electrified 2.86 crore willing households; 2.82 crore was an older figure (March 2021).

na825432cdad.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about floating solar power in India?
o: India's estimated floating-solar potential is about 102 GW
The 278 MW Omkareshwar project is in Andhra Pradesh
Existing floating-solar capacity is about 0.7 GW
Omkareshwar is the largest identified floating solar project
na825432cdad.x: The 278 MW Omkareshwar project is in Madhya Pradesh.

n4882cb40a26.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Tata Renewable hybrid project in Andhra Pradesh?
o: It has 400 MW of solar at Pathikonda
It has 400 MW of wind at Kanekallu
n4882cb40a26.x: The project has 400 MW solar at Pathikonda (Kurnool) and 400 MW wind at Kanekallu (Anantapur).

n638ffd4cab6.s:
Assertion (A): India's installed pumped-storage capacity is approximately 7 GW.
Reason (R): India's pumped-storage potential includes about 58 GW on-stream and 209 GW off-stream.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n638ffd4cab6.x: Both figures are correct, but the size of the potential does not explain the installed capacity.

n2123f857c99.s: Which of the following is wrongly matched?
o: Pulicat – Brackish-water lagoon on the AP–Tamil Nadu border
Kolleru – Brackish-water lagoon on the AP–Tamil Nadu border
Coringa – Mangrove-estuary wildlife sanctuary in the Godavari delta
Eastern Ghats – Tropical forests grading into thorn forests on the Rayalaseema plateau
n2123f857c99.x: Kolleru is a freshwater lake between the Godavari and Krishna deltas; the brackish lagoon is Pulicat.

n085354031d8.s: Which of the following ecologists is wrongly matched?
o: F.E. Clements – Coined the term ecosystem
H.C. Cowles – Succession on Lake Michigan sand dunes
A.G. Tansley – Coined the term ecosystem
n085354031d8.x: Clements is known for phases of succession and the monoclimax theory; Tansley coined 'ecosystem'.

nenvironment-34-8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about ecosystem productivity?
o: Primary productivity is at the autotroph level
Secondary productivity is at the autotroph level
Mangroves are among the most productive ecosystems
Open oceans are among the least productive ecosystems
nenvironment-34-8.x: Secondary productivity is at the consumer (heterotroph) level.

nbiology-61-5.s: Which of the following is wrongly matched?
o: Cyanobacteria – Photosynthetic prokaryotes, many fixing nitrogen
Methanogens – Anaerobic wetlands and ruminant digestive tract
nbiology-61-5.x: Protists are unicellular eukaryotes of water and moist places, some parasitic.

nenvironment-25-8.s: Which of the following is wrongly matched?
o: Ecological footprint – Human demand on Earth's ecosystems
Global hectare – Unit of ecological footprint
Biogeochemical cycle – Movement of nutrient elements through ecosystem components
Anthropogenic biome – Movement of nutrient elements through ecosystem components
nenvironment-25-8.x: An anthropogenic biome (anthrome) is a human-altered terrestrial biosphere; nutrient movement is a biogeochemical cycle.

n7a5273f947a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about producers in ecosystems?
o: At deep-sea vents, chemosynthetic sulphur bacteria are the producers
In terrestrial ecosystems, herbs, shrubs and trees are producers
In aquatic ecosystems, zooplankton are the main producers
In aquatic ecosystems, phytoplankton and algae are producers
n7a5273f947a.x: Zooplankton are primary consumers; aquatic producers are phytoplankton, algae and submerged and floating plants.

na9393d07a54.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about ecosystem stability?
o: Resistance is the ability of an ecosystem to recover after a disturbance
Returning to the earlier condition after a forest fire shows resilience
Homeostasis is self-regulation through feedback up to a limit
Resistance is the ability to withstand a disturbance without change
na9393d07a54.x: Recovering after a disturbance is resilience; resistance is withstanding it without change.

n473f1a0f434.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the components of an ecosystem?
o: Fire and gravity may function as abiotic factors
Parasites and symbionts are abiotic components
Topography and wind are abiotic components
n473f1a0f434.x: Parasites and symbionts are living, biotic components.

n675c94dfb73.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about oceanic productivity?
o: Open oceans have low net primary productivity per unit area
The total output of oceans is large because of their extensive area
Tropical rainforests are more productive per unit area than open oceans
Oceans are the most productive ecosystems per unit area
n675c94dfb73.x: Per unit area, open oceans are low in productivity; tropical rainforests and some aquatic ecosystems are more productive.

nf9eb63d6cc5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about r-selected and K-selected species?
o: Elephants and humans commonly show K-selected characteristics
K-selected species produce few large offspring with considerable parental care
nf9eb63d6cc5.x: Weeds, like insects, commonly show r-selected characteristics.

n013fbf155a8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about population growth?
o: An S-shaped curve shows logistic growth levelling off at carrying capacity K
Carrying capacity is the maximum population an environment can sustain
A J-shaped curve shows exponential growth with unlimited resources
A J-shaped curve shows growth that levels off at carrying capacity
n013fbf155a8.x: The J-curve is exponential growth (dN/dt = rN); levelling off at K belongs to the S-curve.

nacdb48b44e4.x: Saprotrophs feed on dead matter; reptiles are cold-blooded, humans omnivores and camels desert-adapted.

n4ac2a29ba1a.s: The relationship between a tiger and a deer is an example of:
n4ac2a29ba1a.x: Tiger and deer illustrate predation, not competition.

na0721063f1c.s: Which organisms receive no place in ecological pyramids despite their vital role?
na0721063f1c.x: Ecological pyramids omit saprophytes and decomposers; they also cannot place one species at two trophic levels.

n922c0b4e0e2.s: Which ecogeographic rule relates colder climates with shorter ears and limbs?
n922c0b4e0e2.x: Allen's rule concerns appendage length; Bergmann's concerns body size and Rensch's sexual size dimorphism.

ncfbe41024e2.s: Nutrients, water and air form which component of the environment?
ncfbe41024e2.x: Nutrients, water and air form the physical component; carbon and nitrogen cycles are its chemical interactions.

nbiology-61-8.s: Lithophytes are plants that grow on:
nbiology-61-8.x: Lithophytes grow on rocks; hydrophytes grow in water and epiphytes on other plants for support.

n83b3cf273ea.s: Which of the following is NOT a natural terrestrial ecosystem?
n83b3cf273ea.x: Tundra, forest, grassland, desert and mountain are terrestrial ecosystems; an estuary is aquatic.

n6c2193d98c2.s: Gross primary productivity minus producer respiration is called:
n6c2193d98c2.x: NPP is GPP minus producer respiration; secondary productivity is new organic matter formed by consumers.

n507a8656d20.s: A thick cuticle, sunken stomata and CAM are features of:
n507a8656d20.x: These are xerophyte (desert) features; hydrophytes have a thin cuticle, aerenchyma, reduced roots and floating leaves.

nbiology-61-2-14.s: A lichen is a symbiotic association of:
nbiology-61-2-14.x: Lichen is fungus with algae or cyanobacteria; fungus with plant roots is mycorrhiza.

nenvironment-29-4.s: Which biogeochemical cycle begins with rock weathering?
nenvironment-29-4.x: The phosphorus cycle starts with rock weathering; the water cycle is driven by solar energy.

nbiology-53-7.s: Plants that send deep roots down to groundwater are called:
nbiology-53-7.x: Phreatophytes have deep roots reaching groundwater; hydrophytes have buoyant aerenchyma.

n5fb7c3a79c7.s: The Veld grassland is found in:
n5fb7c3a79c7.x: Veld is in South Africa; Prairie is North America, Pampas Argentina and Downs Australia.

n76e7e6b50dd.s: A detritus food chain begins with:
n76e7e6b50dd.x: Detritus chains begin with dead organic matter; grazing chains begin with living green plants.

nenvironment-31-4.s: Secondary consumers occupy which trophic level?
nenvironment-31-4.x: Producers are 1st, primary consumers 2nd, secondary consumers 3rd and top carnivores 4th.

nd4bda069f2b.s: The open water column of the ocean is called the:
nd4bda069f2b.x: The open water column is the pelagic zone; the benthic zone is the sea floor and its organisms.

n811e6e03289.s: The principal decomposers in an ecosystem are:
n811e6e03289.x: Bacteria and fungi are the main decomposers whose enzymes carry out catabolism; earthworms, nematodes and arthropods are helpers.

nf94f991aba6.s: The Nallamala and Seshachalam forests, home to tigers, leopards, sloth bears and elephants, are part of the:
nf94f991aba6.x: Nallamala and Seshachalam are Eastern Ghats forests that provide habitat for tigers, leopards, sloth bears and elephants.

ndf8a68b9408.s: Which of the following are functions of wetlands?
o: Water purification and carbon storage only
Flood moderation, water purification, biodiversity conservation and carbon storage
ndf8a68b9408.x: Wetlands moderate floods, purify water, conserve biodiversity and store carbon.

n1db5895986c.s: Soil texture, pH and minerals are ____ factors.
n1db5895986c.x: Edaphic factors relate to soil; climatic are light, temperature and rainfall, and topographic are altitude, slope and aspect.

ncf311c9c019.s: The main invasive threat to the Banni grassland of Kutch is:
ncf311c9c019.x: The invasive threat named for Banni is Prosopis juliflora, not Lantana camara.

na6a6b6b9556.s: Which of the following does NOT occupy the first trophic level?
na6a6b6b9556.x: Zooplankton are primary consumers at the second level; phytoplankton, seaweeds and green plants are producers.

nenvironment-25-4.x: Eduard Suess coined 'biosphere' (1875); Tansley coined 'ecosystem' and Dasmann 'biological diversity'.

n54bbf9149cf.s: Energy flow in an ecosystem is:
n54bbf9149cf.x: Energy flows in one direction and obeys the laws of thermodynamics; nutrients, not energy, are cycled.

n98eeb6bad44.s: Which of the following is a cold desert?
n98eeb6bad44.x: Ladakh and the Gobi are cold deserts; the Thar of western Rajasthan and Kutch is a hot desert.

nca65e72e59a.s: Which of the following may exist even in the absence of life?
nca65e72e59a.x: A habitat always has life and suits a particular species, whereas the environment may exist without life.

nbiology-53-8.x: Cuscuta is a parasitic flowering plant; the pitcher plant is insectivorous.

o: Western Ghats of Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu
Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha
Himalayan foothills of Uttarakhand and Assam
ndece43c596d.x: Shola occurs in the Western Ghats; the tall wet Terai grasslands lie along the Himalayan foothills.

nf2ab92df610.s: India became a party to the Ramsar Convention in:
nf2ab92df610.x: India joined in 1982; the Convention was signed in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran.

n0d7ad132808.s: The law stating that growth is limited by the nutrient in shortest supply is:
n0d7ad132808.x: Liebig's law; Shelford's law of tolerance says both too little and too much of a factor can limit an organism.

nc932b011c1c.s: A large tree shading a small plant is an example of:
nc932b011c1c.x: It is amensalism (-/0); a lichen is mutualism and the cattle egret near cattle is commensalism.

nbiology-61-20.s: Which of the following is a stem parasite?
nbiology-61-20.x: Cuscuta is a stem parasite; Nepenthes is insectivorous.

nd213158eeab.x: Eutrophic lakes are nutrient-rich and may develop algal blooms; oxygen at depth is often low.

naf4cd203575.s: On average, the total primary production efficiency of an ecosystem is about ____ of incoming solar energy.
naf4cd203575.x: Only about 1–2% of incoming solar energy is captured in photosynthesis; 10% is the share passed between trophic levels.

ne7b4ebce995.s: Which of the following does NOT belong to the physical category of the environment?
ne7b4ebce995.x: Lithosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere are physical; microbes are biotic.

o: Fast decay and highly fertile soil
Thin, nutrient-poor soil due to fast decay
Slow decay, thick litter and acidic soil
n6a53bd4d3e4.x: Taiga has slow decay, thick litter and acidic soil; fast decay and thin, poor soil mark tropical rainforests.

n120732b839c.s: Which of the following is correct about habitat and environment?
o: A habitat can contain only one species
Habitat is a broader concept than environment
n120732b839c.x: A habitat is a particular place within the broader environment, so all habitats are environments; one habitat may contain many species.

nb73d008cb8a.s: All the populations of different species living in an area together form a:
nb73d008cb8a.x: That is a community; a biome is a large region defined by climate and dominant vegetation.

n27a252a5219.s: Hydrilla is an example of a:
n27a252a5219.x: Hydrilla is an aquatic plant (hydrophyte); Opuntia is a xerophyte and Rhizophora a halophyte.

n3cea8f234cf.s: Mature forests provide little net oxygen because:
o: They are no longer carbon sinks
n3cea8f234cf.x: In mature forests respiration roughly balances photosynthesis, though they remain important carbon sinks.

nbiology-53-18.s: Plants associated with saline habitats and salt tolerance are called:
nbiology-53-18.x: Halophytes tolerate salt; xerophytes reduce water loss in deserts and phreatophytes root deep to groundwater.

n1d66301dc99.s: The functional role ('profession') of a species in its habitat is called its:
n1d66301dc99.x: The niche is a species' functional role; it is unique to each species.

n279eb8d7d21.s: Steppe is the temperate grassland of:
n279eb8d7d21.x: Steppe is the Eurasian temperate grassland; Australia's grasslands are the Downs.

nenvironment-3-5.s: World Wetlands Day, marking the signing of the Ramsar Convention, is observed on:
nenvironment-3-5.x: The Ramsar Convention was signed on 2 February 1971, which is observed as World Wetlands Day.

nenvironment-34-10.s: The niche concept is associated with:
nenvironment-34-10.x: Grinnell introduced the niche concept; Tansley coined 'ecosystem'.

nenvironment-34-4.s: When energy passes from one trophic level to the next, only about ____ is transferred.
nenvironment-34-4.x: Only about 10% of energy passes upward, so energy decreases at each level and flows one way.

nenvironment-36-15.s: Which of the following pollutants undergoes biomagnification along food chains?
nenvironment-36-15.x: Mercury builds up along food chains (biomagnification).

nenvironment-34-6.s: An ecosystem, which exchanges energy and matter with its surroundings, is a(n):
nenvironment-34-6.x: An ecosystem is an open system, made of abiotic parts, producers, consumers and decomposers.

nenvironment-33-12.s: Which of the following is true of an ecosystem?
o: It has a fixed universal boundary
It cycles nutrients and has its own productivity
nenvironment-33-12.x: An ecosystem cycles nutrients, has its own productivity and has no fixed universal boundary.

nenvironment-34-7.x: Herbivores are on the second level; top carnivores occupy the highest.

nenvironment-25-7.s: Ponds, lakes and swamps are examples of:
nenvironment-25-7.x: Ponds, lakes and swamps are lentic (still water); rivers and streams are lotic (flowing water).

nfa1a70723c7.s: In the carbon cycle, CO₂ is taken up from the atmosphere by:
nfa1a70723c7.x: Photosynthesis takes up CO₂, while respiration, decay and combustion release it.

nbiology-61-2-11.s: Each fig species is pollinated by its own specific:
nbiology-61-2-11.x: The fig association is a highly specific pollination relationship between a fig and a specific wasp.

nenvironment-25-9.s: The breaking of a continuous habitat into smaller isolated patches is called:
nenvironment-25-9.x: Habitat fragmentation breaks continuous habitat into small isolated patches.

nbiology-62-13.x: Lichens are sensitive to SO₂ and so indicate air pollution.

n20728a0f6ac.s: Open Natural Ecosystems cover over 10% of India, but what share of them is protected?
n20728a0f6ac.x: Open Natural Ecosystems cover more than 10% of India, but less than 5% of them are protected.

n03d99637804.s: Energy flow and nutrient cycling, which underlie productivity and ecosystem services, are aspects of:
n03d99637804.x: Ecosystem function includes processes such as energy flow and nutrient cycling, which support productivity and services.
